actions.justification: MANDATORY - Hour-1 Bundle requires blood cultures BEFORE antibiotic administration. Patient already has positive blood cultures per history but current cultures needed to guide therapy. Must be done first per SSC guidelines.

MANDATORY - Hour-1 Bundle requires serum lactate measurement immediately. Lactate guides resuscitation strategy; if ≥4 mmol/L, aggressive fluid resuscitation required. Patient is hypotensive with MAP 67.

MANDATORY - Administer broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour of sepsis recognition per SSC guidelines. Patient has vancomycin allergy (red man syndrome) so an alternative gram-positive agent (e.g., daptomycin or linezolid) must be selected along with gram-negative coverage. Initiate immediately after blood cultures are drawn.

Patient has hypotension (BP 92/55, MAP 67) meeting criteria for septic shock. SSC Hour-1 Bundle mandates 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid bolus for hypotension. This is the next critical resuscitation step now that cultures and antibiotics are complete.

Evaluate for end-organ dysfunction (renal, hepatic, coagulation, neurologic) to determine severity of sepsis, guide vasopressor/additional therapy decisions, and establish baseline for monitoring response to resuscitation.

Identify the source of gram-positive bacteremia (e.g., endocarditis, line infection, skin/soft tissue, pneumonia) to guide source control measures and optimize antibiotic coverage, particularly given the vancomycin allergy requiring alternative agents.

Serial vital sign assessment is essential to monitor response to fluid resuscitation and determine if MAP target ≥65 mmHg is being maintained. Patient remains tachycardic (HR 108) with borderline MAP (67) and hypotension (BP 92/55).

SSC guidelines recommend vasopressors (norepinephrine as first-line) if patient is hypotensive during or after fluid resuscitation to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg. Patient has septic shock with BP 92/55 and borderline MAP of 67 — vasopressor support is indicated to ensure adequate perfusion pressure.

CBC is needed to assess white blood cell count (infection severity), hemoglobin (oxygen carrying capacity given SpO2 95%), and platelets (coagulopathy/DIC screening) as part of organ dysfunction evaluation in sepsis.
Initial lactate was 4.2 mmol/L (>2 mmol/L), SSC guidelines recommend serial lactate measurements to guide resuscitation and assess treatment response.
Patient remains hypotensive (MAP 67, HR 108) after fluids and vasopressor initiation; reassess perfusion status to evaluate response to resuscitation and guide further management.
BMP needed to assess renal function, electrolytes, and glucose in the setting of septic shock with elevated lactate and ongoing hemodynamic instability.
Patient is on vasopressors (norepinephrine) and requires reliable central venous access for vasopressor infusion, CVP monitoring, and ongoing resuscitation in septic shock.
Continuous arterial blood pressure monitoring is essential given persistent hemodynamic instability (MAP borderline at 67, HR 108) and ongoing vasopressor therapy to titrate resuscitation accurately.
Lactate is 4.2 and patient has septic shock with gram-positive bacteremia; coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen) are indicated to assess for DIC and guide management.

Patient has lactate of 4.2 mmol/L and ongoing hypotension (MAP 67, BP 92/55). Additional crystalloid bolus is indicated to continue resuscitation beyond the initial 30mL/kg, guided by reassessment of perfusion and response to fluids per SSC guidelines.

Patient has fever, tachypnea (RR 22), SpO2 95%, and gram-positive cocci bacteremia. Chest X-ray is indicated to evaluate for pneumonia, empyema, or other pulmonary source of infection, and to assess for pulmonary edema given ongoing fluid resuscitation.

Procalcitonin is useful for monitoring severity of bacterial infection, guiding antibiotic stewardship, and tracking response to therapy in sepsis per SSC guidelines. Baseline value will help guide duration of antibiotic therapy.

Patient remains in septic shock with MAP 67 (borderline) and HR 108, already on norepinephrine. Vasopressin is recommended as an adjunct vasopressor in septic shock to either raise MAP to target or to reduce norepinephrine dosage. Additionally, patient has vancomycin allergy (red man syndrome) and is on broad-spectrum antibiotics — vasopressin addition is appropriate per SSC guidelines when norepinephrine alone is insufficient to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg.
Patient has septic shock with lactate 4.2, MAP 67 on vasopressors, HR 108, RR 22, SpO2 95% — meets criteria for ICU-level care for close hemodynamic monitoring and ongoing resuscitation.
